sources.title: Official GLM-4.7 family API guide
sources.evidence: The separately named GLM-4.7-FlashX tab specifies text input/output, 200K context and 128K maximum output, and positions it as a lightweight high-speed paid option. The page documents thinking and function calling, but does not identify its checkpoint, architecture or parameter counts.

sources.title: Official Chinese GLM-4.7 API guide
sources.evidence: The exact FlashX section independently lists text input/output and 200K context. Family capability documentation includes thinking and function calling. No model-parameter or topology disclosure is supplied for FlashX.

sources.title: Native BigModel Chat Completion API specification
sources.evidence: The native TextChatCompletionRequest model enum explicitly includes glm-4.7-flashx, separately from glm-4.7-flash; its schema accepts thinking controls and function tools. This verifies the hosted interface, not weights or topology.

sources.title: Official API prices
sources.evidence: Lists GLM-4.7-FlashX as a paid text API model separately from the free GLM-4.7-Flash entry. Price/service labels do not prove identical underlying checkpoints.

sources.title: Original January 19 GLM-4.7-Flash launch post
sources.evidence: Native X syndication and oEmbed confirm the original Z.ai author, introduction of GLM-4.7-Flash and publication at 2026-01-19T14:44:34Z, but truncate the long post. Full developer-authored text was retrieved through the mirror in s6: after linking Flash weights, the API section lists free Flash and high-speed paid FlashX. This establishes FlashX launch availability; it does not explicitly say that both names serve identical weights.

sources.title: Full text mirror of original Z.ai launch post
sources.evidence: The complete original launch text lists GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.7-FlashX as API options, with Flash free at one concurrency and FlashX high-speed and affordable. Native X independently corroborates author, post ID, date and opening text; the FlashX suffix of the long post is available through this mirror.

sources.title: Official Z.ai public checkpoint inventory
sources.evidence: The accessed inventory includes GLM-4.7, GLM-4.7-FP8 and GLM-4.7-Flash, with no exact GLM-4.7-FlashX checkpoint. An absent exact name cannot rule out all aliases or undiscovered releases.

sources.title: Related GLM-4.7-Flash model card
sources.evidence: Explicitly describes Flash as 30B-A3B MoE under MIT, but does not mention FlashX or map its API to the published checkpoint. The frozen catalog linked this different named checkpoint; its count, architecture and license cannot be transferred to FlashX without direct identity evidence.

sources.title: Later GLM-5 technical report
sources.evidence: Checked the original later technical report for an exact FlashX comparison or architecture mapping. It does not mention FlashX; the parameter discussion and comparison table concern other named GLM models, so they do not establish FlashX total or active counts.

sources.title: Original developer model download comparison
sources.evidence: The accessed developer download table and README identify named open GLM models but contain no FlashX entry or explicit same-checkpoint relationship. Also checked the GLM-4.7 and GLM-5 model cards for later comparisons; neither mentions FlashX.

sources.title: Z.ai API Terms of Use
sources.evidence: The API terms reserve ownership of model parameters, algorithms, code and framework to Z.ai. This supports proprietary as a description of the hosted API terms; it does not negate any separately proven open checkpoint license.

sources.title: Original Vercel gateway FlashX service page
sources.evidence: The exact FlashX provider page explicitly gives January 19, 2026 as the release date and 200,000 context in its embedded service metadata, corroborating the original launch post and native 200K label. Its generic open-weights metadata is not an exact checkpoint mapping and is not used to establish weight access.

sources.title: PoliLegalLM original comparison and local-evaluation protocol
sources.publisher: PoliLegalLM research team (Zhejiang University, Tongyi Lab and Zhejiang political/legal information center)
sources.evidence: Table 3 labels GLM-4.7-FlashX as 30B/A3B, Local Yes, with a PoliLegal score. Appendix A.3 restricts that private benchmark to locally deployable models. Section 5.1.3, references and linked prompt supplement provide no FlashX checkpoint or API identifier resolving possible confusion with open GLM-4.7-Flash. Table 4 also misstates GLM-5 active parameters as 30B rather than the developer's 40B (s15). The FlashX nominal-count claim is recorded but its model identity is not sufficiently established.

sources.title: Official GLM-4.7-Flash open-source launch
sources.evidence: The developer explicitly reports GLM-4.7-Flash at 30B total and 3B active and links its open weights. The complete launch text does not mention FlashX or identify it as an unchanged variant of the named Flash model. These are supported Flash specifications, not a FlashX disclosure.

sources.title: Official GLM-5 card used to check comparison-table accuracy
sources.evidence: The introduction explicitly states 744B total and 40B active parameters for GLM-5, contradicting the 744B/A30B entry in PoliLegalLM Table 4. This establishes a concrete parameter-metadata error in the comparison source; it supplies no FlashX count.

developer.note: Native Z.ai/Zhipu launch and API documentation.

family.note: Catalog family label for the explicitly named GLM Flash branch; not an architecture or checkpoint-identity assertion.

release_date.note: The original dated launch post lists FlashX among the available API options. Native syndication confirms the January 19 date; the complete long-post suffix is preserved by the cited mirror. Vercel explicitly corroborates this release day. The Flash checkpoint upload date is not used as the basis.

open_weights.note: No exact FlashX checkpoint or explicit primary mapping to the MIT Flash checkpoint was verified. The baseline true assertion is cleared. Its API grouping with Flash is suggestive but does not by itself establish identical weights; absence from an inventory does not prove that no weights exist.

license.note: Classification of the native hosted API terms. The MIT license on the differently named Flash checkpoint is not transferred.

parameters_b.note: The original PoliLegalLM team labels FlashX 30B, but its local-only evaluation protocol leaves the comparison model identity ambiguous; the linked supplement does not resolve it. Fresh developer guides, launch text and checkpoint inventory establish no FlashX count or explicit named-base relationship. The supported 30B Flash nominal size is preserved as comparison evidence rather than transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: PoliLegalLM labels the FlashX comparison A3B, but the unresolved local-model identity and a demonstrable GLM-5 active-count error prevent treating this as a verified FlashX convention. Fresh developer sources report 3B active for Flash only; no FlashX disclosure or explicit lineage supporting its transfer was found.

architecture.note: Native documents describe speed and intended use, without an exact dense/MoE/attention topology. Later original research and download comparisons checked do not map FlashX to Flash or another checkpoint; no sibling architecture is inferred.

context_window.note: Native FlashX tab states 200K; exact provider service metadata specifies 200,000. This is the documented hosted limit, not the 202,752 configured capacity of the separately published Flash checkpoint.

modalities.note: Exact native FlashX tab explicitly specifies text input and text output.

reasoning.note: Native family guide documents thinking; exact FlashX identifier is accepted by the text-completion schema with enabled/disabled thinking controls.

tool_call.note: Native guide documents function calling and the exact text API schema accepts FlashX with function tools. Tool streaming is a separate capability and is not inferred.

description.value: Hosted GLM text model with optional reasoning and function calling.
description.note: Neutral supported interface description; removes unsupported comparative performance and efficiency claims.

patch.description: Hosted GLM text model with optional reasoning and function calling.
patch.notes: GLM-4.7-FlashX is a paid high-speed text API with a 200,000-token context. Total and active parameters remain unverified: PoliLegalLM lists 30B/3B, but its local-model description leaves possible confusion with the separate Flash checkpoint unresolved. No developer statement mapping FlashX to that checkpoint was established. Open-weight status remains unverified; proprietary describes the hosted API terms.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit found an original 30B/A3B FlashX comparison label, but could not establish which locally deployable model it identifies. Retain null total and active counts with unverified status, documenting the claim and the unresolved identity. Current native guides, the official Flash launch/card, the public checkpoint inventory and the later GLM-5 report supply no FlashX count or explicit named-base mapping. All twelve other field assessments are preserved.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Both parameters_b and active_parameters_b remain null; change assessment status to unverified to acknowledge an original but identity-ambiguous 30B/A3B comparison claim.

fresh_originals.finding: Complete native guide: separately named lightweight/high-speed FlashX, no parameter count or named Flash base relationship.
Complete Chinese guide: FlashX positioned as lightweight high-speed version, without an explicit named base or count.
Fresh full-text mirror: 30B wording names Flash; FlashX appears separately in the API-options list, without an explicit same-model/variant statement.
Developer nominal 30B-A3B describes Flash; card does not mention FlashX.
Official launch independently supplies Flash total and active counts, but no FlashX lineage.
No exact FlashX entry in fresh developer inventory; absence is not proof that no alias exists.
Later developer report checked for FlashX comparison/lineage; no FlashX occurrence.
Read baseline section, both comparison tables, references, local-only private-benchmark protocol and supplement link; ambiguous local FlashX identity remains.
Independent developer evidence of the comparison table's GLM-5 active-count error.
Author-linked supplement record resolves to 19444016 and lists only prompt.md.
Read linked prompt template; no baseline identifier, checkpoint or deployment information.
Bounded exact-name repository lookup returned total_count=0; no original evaluation code identified.

parameter_reaudit.reasoning: Nominal comparison figures and named unchanged variant lineage are acceptable evidence; no exact tensor census or hosting attestation was demanded. Here the paper names FlashX but describes and evaluates it as a local model without resolving which checkpoint it means. The sole linked supplement and repository search did not resolve that identity, and a separate active-count error weakens the metadata. Developer sources name Flash at 30B/3B and separately list FlashX without explicitly naming its base. No supported FlashX lineage was established, so no structural-change inference can be completed. Secondary gateway descriptions that repeat Flash text were discovery leads only.
